ATTACHMENT A
Type 1 Rezoning Project Narrative — 3750 W North Avenue

The Applicant proposes a Type 1 rezoning of the property located at 3750 W North Avenue, Chicago,
Illinois from RT-4 (Residential Two-Flat, Townhouse and Multi-Unit District) to C1-2 (Neighborhood
Commercial District) to allow for the adaptive reuse of the property as a custom design and fabrication
studio specializing in handmade fumiture, custom cabinetry, and architectural installations. The business
integrates woodworking and metalworking techniques to produce refined, functional pieces, and will use
the space for both small-scale production and retail showroom purposes.

The project will not involve any new construction, additions, or expansion of the existing building. The

Applicant will maintain the existing structure, footprint, and site layout. No residential uses are proposed.

Interior improvements are planned, including the demolition of a small existing office and the partitioning
of the interior into two equal spaces, each approximately 2,000 square feet. The northern portion will be
occupied by the Applicant, who will install workbenches and stationary light-industrial equipment to
support its fabrication needs. These operations will remain entirely indoors and low impact in nature. The
Applicant anticipates to hopefully add up to two full-time employees as a result of the relocation and
business expansion. The Applicant will refresh the interior layout to create a flexible second space that can
ideally be leased to a complementary local business, fostering collaboration and supporting neighborhood
entrepreneurship. By adapting the existing building rather than expanding it, these thoughtful improvements
promote small-scale manufacturing alongside retail activity and ensure the property continues to strengthen
and enliven the North Avenue. Applicant has already proactively contacted groups such as the Greater West
Town Community Development Project and the Puerto Rican Cultural Center to gauge interest in the space.
While neither organization expressed interest, the Applicant intends to prioritize its existing network of
artists and craftspeople when seeking a tenant and is already in discussions with several prospective
candidates. If alignment cannot be reached with an artisan tenant, the space may be leased to a local
tradesperson such as a general contractor, electrician, or plumber, or potentially used for small-scale storage
or shop operations, depending on what zoning will allow. This approach reflects the Applicant’s
commitment to supporting local enterprise and contributing to a resilient, mixed-use commercial corridor.

As part of the buildout, the Applicant wil] install ceiling insulation, upgrade the HVAC system, replace the
north-facing overhead door, and increase the electrical service capacity to 240V, 3-phase power. These
upgrades will modernize the facility without altering the building’s exterior character, and will support
responsible reactivation of underutilized space.

The building’s front masonry facade will remain unaltered, consistent with the surrounding streetscape. The
Applicant does not plan to install signage that require permitting but understands that any future tenant
wishing to do so will be responsible for obtaining the necessary permits. A planter will be placed at the
front of the building to increase curb appeal, and the rear yard will be cleared and maintained. Refuse will
be stored in the rear yard or alley and will be secured as is customary in the area. Applicant intends to
coordinate with neighbors to manage shared alley access and security.

The rear yard will be retained for employee and occasional client parking, with no anticipated need for
street parking on North Avenue. Parking allocation for any future tenant will be addressed as part of the
lease terms.

Project Details:
e Proposed Land Use:

Custom design and fabrication studio with on-site showroom for the sale of handmade furniture,
custom cabinetry, and architectural installations. Use includes light fabrication (wood and metal)
and retail sales. If possible, a portion of the building will be leased to a local future commercial
tenant.

e Floor Area Ratio (FAR):

The existing FAR is approximately 0.632, as the property consists of a one-story commercial
building with an approximate building area of 3,995 square feet on a lot of 6,319 square feet total
area, There is no change to FAR proposed.

e Density (Lot Area per Dwelling Unit):
Not applicable. This project proposes no residential dwelling units.
e Off-Street Parking:

The property has approximately 2,324 square foot gated surface lot of on-site parking at the rear,
accommodating up to eight vehicles, which will remain unchanged. The parking ratio is 0.93/1,000
sq. ft. The parking lot will be used by the Applicant and any future tenant as needed. Customers
rarely frequent the facility so they should be reasonably accommodated with the spaces provided.
No additional parking is proposed or required under the C1-2 designation.

e Setbacks:

The building maintains its existing legal non-conforming setbacks, consistent with commercial
buildings along North Avenue. No changes to setbacks are proposed. The approximate setbacks
are:

o Front Yard: 0 feet
o Side Yards: 0 feet (lot line to lot line construction)
o Rear Yard: 0 feet, used for parking and loading.

e Building Dimensions:

The existing building is a one-story structure with an overall height of approximately 20 feet. It
contains two drive-in loading doors: one on the south side measuring 12 feet 4 inches in height by
14 feet in width, and one on the north side measuring 11 feet 9 inches in height by 10 feet in width.
The warehouse interior measures approximately 48 feet (east to west) by 78 feet 6 inches (north to
south), with a clear height of 14 feet 5 inches to the bottom of the beams and 16 feet 7 inches from
floor to ceiling. No changes to the building dimensions are proposed.

Site Plan & Illustrative Details (Type 1 Visual Submittals)

The Applicant will submit a site plan and existing conditions drawings to accompany this narrative.
These will illustrate:

e Building Location, Orientation, and Setbacks:

The building is located at the front of the lot with a 0-foot front yard setback, facing North Avenue,
consistent with neighboring commercial properties. Side yard setbacks are 0 feet, and the rear yard
provides parking and access.

e Building Bulk and Scale in Relation to Nearby Buildings:

The existing structure is a single-story commercial building, which is consistent with adjacent and
nearby commercial and mixed-use buildings along North Avenue. The scale is similar to the
neighbors and appropriately fits the corridor’s context. Names:

e Location of Curb Cuts, Sidewalks, and Loading:

The property utilizes an existing rear alley and attached curb cut for vehicle access to the parking
spaces at the rear of the building. No changes are proposed to the sidewalk or curb configuration.
Loading and deliveries will occur from the rear, using the existing access.

e Landscaping and On-Site Open Space:

The property is improved consistent with neighborhood commercial properties. The existing paved.
rear yard provides parking and loading access. Applicant will add a planter to the front of the
building but otherwise, no additional landscaping or open space is proposed or required for this
use.

¢ Location of Dumpsters or Trash Enclosures:

Trash and recycling will be stored in standard commercial waste containers located at the rear of
the property, screened and in compliance with City code requirements.

Conclusion

This proposed Type 1 rezoning allows for the adaptive reuse of an existing building in a manner that
supports small business growth, neighborhood activation, and thoughtful design and fabrication consistent
with the evolving commercial character of the corridor. The improvements will preserve the building’s
existing scale while modernizing the interior for productive and flexible use. The project furthers the goals
of the Zoning Ordinance by promoting active use of commercial space, encouraging local entrepreneurship,
and contributing to the vitality of the North Avenue corridor.
